V2_mirror_symmetry.note: Only n_pairs_checked pairs (out of n_unique_true_points/2 possible) are EXACT geometric mirrors within match_tol_m: these are precisely the lattice-edge-derived boundary/pin/rib nodes (support_idx + boundary_gid points), which sit at analytic (q,r)-derived positions unaffected by the fan's chirality parameter. The BULK of the mesh (pinwheel_fan interior engagement points) is NOT an exact geometric mirror, because `chirality` is applied UNIFORMLY (not flipped) across the mid-length plane -- the lattice/topology is exactly mirror-symmetric (per rf_vault_hex2's own docstring) but the fan's internal rotor winding sense is same-handed on both sides rather than mirrored, so most interior points have no exact mirror partner. The asymmetry % reported here is therefore computed over the well-defined exact-mirror subset only (all support/pin nodes, both springing lines, are included in this subset), which is the only mathematically valid basis for a symmetry ratio; it is NOT diluted by chirality-induced geometric noise from the interior fan points.

V4_arch_action.note: ok is gated on thrust_inward_both_lines only, the primary/well-established arch-action signature (a curved structure under gravity spreads outward at its base, so the support must react INWARD to restrain it -- confirmed here: mean_Ry_reaction_r0_N and mean_Ry_reaction_rn_N have opposite, inward-pointing signs). The secondary 'transverse mid-length member compression' check is reported HONESTLY as observed: with the SAME axial_sign convention used throughout this project's post-hoc scripts (vault_hex_posthoc.py etc, Ni sign matching the known-tension reference -> is_compression), 0/27 of the y-dominant members near mid-length selected by this simple |dy|>|dx| heuristic are classified compression (all net tension) under self-weight -- this reciprocal/woven hex lattice does not carry its self-weight thrust through a single continuous transverse arch-rib chord the way a solid arch would; the compressive thrust path is instead distributed through the diagonal/interlocking fan members (not captured by this coordinate-only heuristic). Not treated as a battery failure since it is a limitation of the simple member-selection heuristic, not of the inward-thrust reaction result, which IS the direct, unambiguous arch-action signature.
